subsystems.name: Light absorber
subsystems.role: captures sunlight and creates the electron–hole pairs that drive the chemistry.

subsystems.name: Oxygen-evolving electrode
subsystems.role: splits water to supply electrons and protons, releasing oxygen.
parts: nickel–iron oxide or cobalt phosphate catalyst

subsystems.name: CO2-reduction electrode
subsystems.role: converts CO2 and protons into carbon monoxide, formate or short hydrocarbons.

subsystems.name: Membrane and electrolyte
subsystems.role: keeps the two half-reactions apart so products do not recombine, and carries ions between them.

subsystems.name: CO2 supply
subsystems.role: delivers concentrated carbon dioxide at the electrode surface, where it is scarce in water.

subsystems.name: Biocatalyst module
subsystems.role: hybrid systems use enzymes or microbes to fix carbon into more complex molecules.

subsystems.name: Product separation and upgrading
subsystems.role: extracts dilute products and turns them into usable fuels or chemicals.

buildSteps.title: Choose the architecture
buildSteps.detail: Either a single photoelectrochemical cell that absorbs light and drives the reaction in one device, or a solar panel wired to a separate electrolyser. The wired route is easier; the integrated route uses less material.

buildSteps.title: Grow the light absorber
buildSteps.detail: Semiconductor layers are deposited on a substrate, often as a tandem stack so each layer absorbs a different part of the spectrum.

buildSteps.title: Protect it from corrosion
buildSteps.detail: Thin oxide or metal coatings and tunnel junctions stop the electrolyte from dissolving the semiconductor — the main reason lab cells die within hours.

buildSteps.title: Deposit the catalysts
buildSteps.detail: Oxygen- and CO2-reducing catalysts are electrodeposited or sputtered onto the electrodes as nanoscale films.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the cell
buildSteps.detail: Electrodes, membrane and electrolyte are stacked into a sealed cell with gas and liquid inlets and outlets.

buildSteps.title: Add biocatalysis if hybrid
buildSteps.detail: Engineered enzymes or microbes are immobilised next to the electrode to take the simple products and build larger molecules.

buildSteps.title: Benchmark under sunlight
buildSteps.detail: The cell runs under a simulated solar spectrum while efficiency, selectivity and lifetime are measured in hours and then thousands of hours.

buildSteps.title: Scale to modules and field-test
buildSteps.detail: Cells are enlarged to tens of square centimetres, grouped into panels, and coupled to a real CO2 stream.

prerequisites.why: benchmark cells exceed 10% solar-to-hydrogen efficiency in the lab, but only for short periods.
copper and silver catalysts reach high selectivity for single products such as carbon monoxide or formate, but not yet for the mix of longer molecules fuels need.
a practical device must survive years in electrolyte under illumination; today's cells last hours to weeks.
the wired PV-plus-electrolyser route already works technically and competes on cost with the integrated version.
the reaction needs far more CO2 than water can dissolve, so capture and delivery dominate both energy and cost.
Rubisco is slow and oxygen-sensitive; engineered and synthetic pathways aim to fix carbon faster.

pathway.milestone: lab cells splitting water and reducing CO2 to carbon monoxide or formate at square-centimetre scale
pathway.unlocks: proof that sunlight can drive carbon chemistry without living plants.

pathway.milestone: modules of tens of square centimetres running for thousands of hours without losing efficiency
pathway.unlocks: the durability data investors and standards bodies need.

pathway.milestone: coupling to industrial CO2 streams to make syngas or formic acid as chemical feedstocks
pathway.unlocks: a first market that does not require competing with bulk fossil fuels on price.

pathway.milestone: drop-in liquid fuels made from captured CO2 and sunlight
pathway.unlocks: low-carbon aviation and shipping fuel — if costs fall below the green-hydrogen-plus-captured-CO2 route.
